physics_goals.quote: An experiment to search for light sterile neutrinos was conducted at a reactor with a thermal power of 2.8 GW
physics_goals.value: Search for light sterile neutrinos at a distance of 24 m from a commercial reactor core, testing the reactor antineutrino anomaly

summary.plain: A one-tonne liquid-scintillator detector placed in a gallery 24 metres from a commercial reactor core in Korea, used to look for a hypothetical sterile neutrino. It ran in 2015-16 and again in 2018-20 and found no sign of oscillation to one.
summary.technical: Short-baseline (23.7 m) reactor antineutrino experiment: ~1 t Gd-loaded liquid scintillator in the tendon gallery of Hanbit unit 5 (2.8 GW_th, low-enriched uranium), 20 m.w.e. overburden. NEOS-I (2015-16, 180 d on / 46 d off) excluded the RAA optimum at > 90 % CL; NEOS-II (2018-20) covered a full fuel cycle; a joint RENO-NEOS spectral analysis gives a 95 % CL exclusion over 0.1-7 eV^2.
